To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inclusion of tumor genotype data in linkage analysis of cancer families can substantially increase the power to detect linkage and to exclude linkage.
the use of tumor genotype data can improve the power of genetic linkage analysis in cancer families.
the use of tumor genotype data in linkage analyses of cancer families can substantially improve the statistical power to detect genetic linkage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of tumor genotype information in linkage analysis of human cancer.
the development and application of statistical methodology to problems in human cancer research.
the development of statistical methods for linkage analysis of cancer families, and the evaluation of these methods by computer simulation studies and by application to real data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is consistent with a single gene, but that the evidence does not support the hypothesis of linkage.
the evidence of linkage is consistent with the hypothesis that the disease locus is located in the 5q31‐q33 region, but that the evidence of nonlinkage cannot be ruled out.
the evidence is not sufficient to support the claim that there are any genetic loci that are associated with a predisposition to develop colon cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
somatic allele loss (SAL) can be used to infer the phase of alleles in the germline and thus increase the power of linkage analysis in cancer families.
we developed a new statistical method that can be used to improve the power to detect genetic linkage in studies involving families of patients with cancer.
the use of tumor tissue in genetic linkage analyses of cancer families is feasible and can substantially increase the power of linkage analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tumor genotype data can be used to improve the power of genetic linkage analysis in families with cancer.

if you have a cancer family with a tumor sample from an affected individual and you can genotype that tumor sample, then you can use the genotype information from the tumor sample to improve the linkage analysis of the family.
